CONTEXT.content: When production breaks, the first minutes matter. Triage means assessing impact, assigning severity, and communicating before you fix.
CONTEXT.analogy: ER triage: stabilize the patient, don't perform surgery in the waiting room.
CONTEXT.productionNote: Teams that skip triage fix the wrong thing while users burn.

DECIDE.optionA: Declare incident immediately and pull everyone into a war room.
DECIDE.optionB: Quietly investigate until you understand scope, then declare if needed.

tradeoffs.A: Fast coordination; alert fatigue if overused.
tradeoffs.B: Less noise; risk of delayed response on real outages.

hints: What signals mean 'page now' vs 'ticket for Monday'?

BUILD.goal: Write an incident runbook section: severity levels (SEV1-3), who to notify, and first 3 diagnostic commands for your app.

tracks.node: Document curl health checks and log grep patterns.

acceptance: Three severity levels with clear criteria
hints: SEV1 = user-visible data loss or full outage.
Runbook should work when you're panicking.

criteria: Peer can classify a sample outage using your runbook
Notification path is realistic for your team size
hints: If only you understand it, it's not a runbook.

BREAK.scenario: Pager fires at 2am. Error rate is 2% — only affects free-tier users. Marketing launch in 6 hours.
BREAK.symptoms: Logs show timeouts on one dependency. Core paid users unaffected.
hints: What's the minimum fix before launch?

FIX.goal: Classify severity, document immediate mitigation (feature flag, circuit breaker, or rollback), and draft a one-line status update.
hints: Communicate what you know and what you don't.

decisionCallbacks.A: Early war room would have aligned comms — but might have over-escalated a 2% free-tier issue.
decisionCallbacks.B: Quiet investigation saved noise — but delayed status page update if it was actually SEV1.
